assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Scientific model
items.clue: An idea used to explain observations; new experimental evidence may lead to a model being changed or replaced.

items.label: Plum pudding model
items.clue: The model that followed the discovery of the electron: the atom is a ball of positive charge with negative electrons embedded in it.

items.label: Simple distillation
items.clue: A physical process that separates a solvent from a solution by boiling it off and condensing the vapour, leaving the dissolved solid behind.

items.label: Compound
items.clue: A substance containing two or more elements chemically combined in fixed proportions, represented by a formula built from the symbols of the atoms it was formed from.

questions.stem: What does the relative atomic mass of an element take account of?

options.text: The abundance of each of its isotopes
The mass number of its commonest isotope
The average of its isotope mass numbers
The number of protons and neutrons combined

questions.explanation: Relative atomic mass is an average that takes account of isotope abundance.

questions.stem: In which order do electrons occupy the energy levels (shells) of an atom?

options.text: The outer shell is filled before the inner ones
They spread out evenly between the shells
The lowest available energy level is filled first
The first shell takes eight electrons first

questions.explanation: Electrons occupy the lowest available energy levels, the innermost available shells.

questions.stem: Lithium has two isotopes: 7.5% is ⁶Li and 92.5% is ⁷Li. What is the relative atomic mass of lithium?
A magnesium atom has 12 electrons. Which electronic structure is correct?
questions.explanation: Two electrons fill the first level and eight the second, leaving two in the third.

questions.stem: The electronic structure of sodium is 2,8,1. What does the final 1 tell you?

options.text: There is one electron in the third energy level
There is one electron in the innermost shell only
One of the shells in the atom is completely full
The last shell was filled up first of all

questions.explanation: The numbers are read outwards, so the last one is the outermost level.

questions.stem: Why is the electronic structure of sodium 2,8,1 rather than 2,9?

options.text: The first energy level always holds eight electrons
The second energy level holds only eight electrons
The outer energy level is always filled up first of all
The numbers are read from the outside of the atom inwards

questions.explanation: Once the second level holds eight, the next electron starts the third level.

questions.stem: A fluorine atom has 9 electrons. Which shell diagram is correct?

options.text: 2 on the first ring and 7 on the second
8 on the first ring and 1 on the second
7 on the first ring and 2 on the second
5 on the first ring and 4 on the second

questions.explanation: The first energy level is full with two electrons, so the other seven go in the second.

questions.stem: A shell diagram is drawn with 4 electrons on the outer ring, 8 on the middle ring and 2 on the inner ring. Which electronic structure does it show?
questions.explanation: The structure starts at the innermost ring: 2, then 8, then 4.
